children: The iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF
fell to its lowest price since May 13, 2004, extending a long-term decline in prices of longer-dated U.S. government bonds.
TLT was down 1.27% at $80.69 on Thursday, according to the Barchart chart.

The move brought the ETF back to a level it had last reached more than two decades ago. The chart showed TLT trading around the low $80s in 2003 and 2004 before beginning a prolonged climb over the following years.

TLT then reached peaks above $170 around 2020, before entering a broad decline. The ETF fell sharply from those highs through 2022 and continued to trade at substantially lower levels over the following years.
The latest decline left TLT near the lower end of its long-term range, with Thursday's $80.69 close sitting almost directly on the level marked on the chart as its May 2004 low.
The move underscored the scale of the longer-term retreat in long-duration Treasury prices, with TLT now back near levels last seen more than 20 years ago.

title: Long-term Treasury ETF TLT falls to lowest level since 2004
